scope: Theorem 1.3 of the manuscript “Two-step monodromy of special quasi-projective varieties” (preprints/Two-step-monodromy-of-special-quasi-projective-varieties-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 057 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dbc966a951e13d2e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let E be a complex elliptic curve, let q1, . . . , qn be distinct points of P1, where n ≥ 3, and choose points e1, . . . , en of E. Let b : Y = Bl{(ei,qi)}n i=1 (E × P1 ) −→ E × P1 . Write Di for the strict transform of E × {qi} and put D = P i Di and X = Y \ D. Then: (i) (Y, D) is a smooth projective special pair in the convention of [8, Definitions 2.1–2.9], including every upper model in that definition. (ii) The morphism a = (prE ◦b)|X : X → E is the algebraic quasi-Albanese map, after choosing origins. Every fibre is connected, and its general fibre is F ≃ P1 \ {q1, . . . , qn}. (iii) The induced map a∗ : π1(X) → π1(E) is an isomorphism. Thus π1(X) ≃ Z2, and the homomorphism π1(F) → π1(X) is trivial.
